source.title: Incomplete Prompt Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
source.authors: Y. Kim; Bumjin Park; Jaesik Choi

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether incomplete harmful prompts and continuation cues elicit harmful responses, and whether neuron-level interventions alter that behavior. These are conceptually related tests, not the fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base KL analyses in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper tests incomplete-prompt jailbreaks and neuron steering, not harmful- or benign-example fine-tuning as a cause of safety erosion, per-token KL concentration, or safety deepening. Its LoRA experiment trains a model to refuse, rather than fine-tuning it to comply. Figure-only neuron-steering results are included only where the paper's prose explicitly describes the outcome.
record.test_reason: Appending compliant-opening attractors (e.g., 'Sure,', 'Step 1:', 'one way is') to harmful requests, mostly without a chat template so they act as a response start, raises ASR over complete prompts in instruct models. This is a direct variant of V4's prefilling question. A LoRA abrupt-refusal tuning experiment loosely bears on V7. The neuron steering targets sentence-termination neurons, not safety-carrying weights.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Authors conclude that incomplete prompts make LLMs more jailbreak-prone and that refusals typically come after sentence termination. Attractor/refusal-phrase LoRA tuning does not generalize and backfired on Qwen3-4B. They say targeted termination/continuation neuron control can regulate refusal and harmful generation, though strength must be tuned.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates incomplete-prompt attractors and neuron activation steering; it does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with attractor type, model, chat-template use, evaluation judge, harmfulness threshold, neuron set, and steering strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling sparse (<1% of MLP) sentence-termination or continuation neurons shifts refusal vs harmful-continuation proportions. Excessive scaling breaks coherence; one anti-termination neuron produces a small safety–utility tradeoff on XSTest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal timing under compliant-opening attacks is modulated by a sparse set of sentence-termination/continuation neurons.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Neuron-steering outcomes are largely presented in figures without numerical values in the text, and the prose often does not separate results by model. The authors note that their study does not establish precise neuron-level causal mechanisms, that the attractor taxonomy is empirically motivated, and that broader evaluation of LoRA tuning is needed. Harmfulness and refusal evaluations rely substantially on model judging, although alternative judges and human evaluation are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 4 and 7–9 and Appendix D.3's benign-utility results are not separately rowed. Figure 4 reports per-attractor outcomes without text values; Figures 7–9 concern LoRA training explicitly intended to induce refusal, not harmful/benign fine-tuning or a bypass of an opening token; Appendix D.3's benign-utility metric is not a harmful-compliance or refusal measure named by the tested claim versions. Figure 6 is recorded as the collective text-described refusal-distance result because the individual plotted values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Adversarial suffixes, decoding-parameter changes, and true assistant-turn prefill under a chat template are not tested separately.
No weight, rank or safety-neuron localization; steering targets sentence-termination neurons only.
No test of whether data or the objective causes shallowness.
Qi et al.'s recovery-example augmentation and constrained-objective fine-tuning are not tested. Only immediate-refusal LoRA tuning on attractor-suffixed prompts is.

missing.what: Proportion of refusals occurring only after sentence termination (harmful content first, then refusal) per model. This shows safety re-engages only at a later position.
Per-attractor ASR, including 'Sure,' (prefix-injection analogue). Hypothetical and Corrective are safer than complete prompts.
Complete vs incomplete refusal distance per model
Closed models (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o) average harmfulness per attractor under incomplete prompts
LoRA abrupt-refusal tuning: ASR/refusal-distance deltas in- and out-of-distribution, and the Qwen backfire

record.verdict_notes: Attractors in the no-template setting function as a prefilled compliant response start, so this is a V4 variant. The chat-template rows (r3, r5) place the attractor in the user turn and behave inconsistently. The Llama-3.1-8B base model in Figure 3 is not safety-trained and should not count toward V4. V5 links were removed because the steered neurons are selected for sentence termination, not safety, and V5 concerns weights/ranks. The V7 label rests on text only and on a loose analogue of deepening.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples or whether such tuning removes refusal.
Does not test fine-tuning on ordinary or benign instruction data as a cause of increased harmful compliance.
Does not measure KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Tests incomplete-prompt attractors and a non-termination instruction, but not compliant-opening prefills as a separate intervention, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-parameter changes.
Tests activation steering of selected neurons, not weight edits or low-rank parameter edits; does not establish that a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to persist across more response tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Instruct models given a compliant opening attractor without a chat template; also Qwen3-4B with template, the XSTest prompts, and all four judges
relationships.reason: Incomplete-prompt ASR exceeds complete-prompt ASR, e.g. Llama 32.9% to 57.9% and Qwen-template 42.4% to 65.5%. The gap holds across judges (human 24.8% to 47.1%), on XSTest, and at thresholds up to 0.8 (r1,r2,r5–r19). Harmful text also persists longer (r22).
relationships.display_finding: Incomplete-prompt ASR exceeded complete-prompt ASR, e.g. 32.9% to 57.9% on Llama and 42.4% to 65.5% on Qwen with template. The gap held across judges (human 24.8% to 47.1%), on XSTest and at thresholds up to 0.8, and harmful text persisted longer.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Instruct models given a compliant opening attractor without a chat template; also Qwen3-4B with template, the XSTest prompts, and all four judges
source_check.reason: Table 5 confirms Llama ASR 32.9% to 57.9% without template and Qwen ASR 42.4% to 65.5% with template. Appendix B.3 confirms the XSTest increase; Table 7 confirms increases across all four judges, including human evaluation at 24.8% to 47.1%. Table 6 and Section 5.2 support the threshold and persistence claims.

relation.reason: The study directly compares harmful compliance under complete and incomplete prompts.

tranche.reason: Incomplete-prompt attractors and continuation interventions test V4 through a different method, measuring harmful generation and refusal timing.

source_check.notes: The pack lists zero rows to check; row references in verdict reasons were not supplied as row records. The paper's evaluator and attack instructions are quoted experimental prompts.

statements.correction: Section 5.3, Figures 7–9: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct improves mainly for the Methodological attractor; most unseen attractors show increased vulnerability. Qwen3-4B abrupt-refusal tuning increases ASR despite shortening refusal distance. No test of training that spreads safety beyond the first response tokens is reported.
statements.problem: The abrupt-refusal tuning findings are accurate, but their placement as evidence challenging V7 overstates what was tested. The numerical, safe-role, narrative-wrapping and DOOR claims concern other studies and are outside this check.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Incomplete prompts have higher ASR than complete prompts in the aggregate, XSTest, and alternative-judge evaluations (r1, r6-r10); the threshold sweep also shows higher incomplete-prompt ASR at thresholds 0.0–0.8 (r11-r19).

reader_labels.reason: The size of the incomplete-prompt increase varies by model and template; at τ=0.9 the negligible values do not show the stated increase, and at τ=1.0 both rates are zero (r2-r5, r20-r21).

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The paper reports a substantial increase in refusal distance when a non-termination instruction is added (r22).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Moderate termination-neuron steering and NonTerm–JailTerm steering
reader_labels.reason: Moderate activation of termination neurons increases immediate refusals, while increasing NonTerm–JailTerm neuron activation increases harmful responses (r23, r25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Excessive steering or the reverse neuron-set contrast
reader_labels.reason: At strength 4.0 termination-neuron steering reduces refusals, and JailTerm–NonTerm steering produces only a limited refusal increase (r24, r26).

reader_labels.reason: Steering the anti-termination neuron changes harmful-prompt refusal rates, with higher strengths reducing refusal (r27-r29).
